Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin 2 is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an AI panel. Its first launch is: welcome screen, then one printer-setup step, then Home. On 2026-11-07 Kenneth Jiang (the owner) decided:
- JusPrin 1 and JusPrin 2 share no account. The only overlap is that JusPrin 2 can import JusPrin 1's printers, presets and printer connections, in a way very similar to the OrcaSlicer import.
- There are three ways to set up printers: import from JusPrin 1, import from OrcaSlicer, or choose a printer by hand. Each of those screens links to the other two, so all three can be found whether the app found anything or not.
- When both JusPrin 1 and OrcaSlicer are found, the JusPrin 1 screen opens first.
- A link to an app that wasn't found opens a folder picker, then that app's import screen.
- File › Import gains "Import from JusPrin 1…" next to "Import from OrcaSlicer…".
- The JusPrin 1 subscriber price is handled manually outside the app, so the app never mentions it.
- He also agreed the app should look for OrcaSlicer in more places.

Today's code contradicts most of this:
- It copies JusPrin 1's data silently at start-up.
- It opens a separate "welcome back" window that checks the JusPrin 1 sign-in.
- It skips the printer step for JusPrin 1 users.
- The printer form mentions no import.

The design is drawn on the canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ (version 149, "On boarding experience" page), and the flow is on https://claude.ai/artifact/LV1mW9VHJvP4skpSyEbcEs. Kenneth wants the code to follow the boards exactly.

Task:
Build the decisions in the background into the JusPrin app. Work in your own worktree, on a branch cut from the local `ui-walkthrough` branch. Commit there. Don't push, and don't touch `ui-walkthrough` itself.

Before you start, read `AGENTS.md`, and also `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` if you change anything outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.

**The boards are the spec.** Read them from the canvas with the Artifact tool. Look at both pictures and text. Do not edit the canvas.
- `project/first-run-19-jusprin1-import.dc.html`: "Bring your printers from JusPrin 1?"
- `project/first-run-20-jusprin1-import-result.dc.html`: "Imported from JusPrin 1"
- `project/first-run-07-orcaslicer-import.dc.html`, `project/first-run-08-add-printer.dc.html` and `project/first-run-18-printer-reading.dc.html`: each now ends with an "Other ways:" line of two links
- `project/orca-import-01-file-menu.dc.html`: the new File › Import item
- `project/first-run-11-flow.dc.html`: the map of the first launch

The canvas notes `first-run-printer-about` and `orca-import-about` in `project/canvas.json` say what is agreed. Screen text says "JusPrin 1", as the boards do.

**What to change** (paths relative to `src/slic3r/GUI/`; line numbers are as of `ui-walkthrough` 2599bc350c):

1. **The JusPrin 1 import is asked first, not done silently.**
   - Stop the copy at start-up (`GUI_App.cpp:2464`, `JusPrin/V1Import/V1Import.cpp`). Keep `v1_folder()` for finding the folder.
   - Keep the import's scope as commit a739dc4e7e set it: only printers, presets and printer connections, plus `BambuNetworkEngine.conf`. Never app settings.
   - The JusPrin 1 printer screen and its result screen should reuse the OrcaSlicer import's code: `JusPrin/Home/OrcaImporter.*`, `AgentUI/src/components/OrcaImportLists.tsx`, and the `OrcaImport` and `ImportResult` parts of `HomeUI/src/components/Onboarding.tsx`. Don't build a second copy; Kenneth's rule is to reuse what exists. Presets reload after the import, as the OrcaSlicer import already does.

2. **Remove the welcome-back window.**
   - Remove `JusPrin/V1Import/WelcomeBackWindow.*`, `AgentUI/src/components/WelcomeBack.tsx` and their JusPrin 1 sign-in check.
   - Remove the trigger that opens the window (`JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp` around lines 967 and 1420).
   - Remove the "Subscribed to JusPrin v1?" line (`Onboarding.tsx:87-89`).
   - Rework what `OnboardingFacts::v1_imported` and `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:430-437` did with the import report.

3. **Choose which printer screen opens** (`JusPrin/Home/OnboardingModel.*`):
   - JusPrin 1 found: the JusPrin 1 screen, even when OrcaSlicer is also found.
   - Only OrcaSlicer found: the OrcaSlicer screen.
   - Neither found: the printer form.
   - A file opened at launch still skips the step.
   - Back still returns to the welcome screen.

4. **Add "Other ways" links on every printer screen**, worded as the boards draw them:
   - The OrcaSlicer screen: "Import from JusPrin 1…" and "Choose my printer". These replace the "Choose my printer instead" button.
   - The JusPrin 1 screen: "Import from OrcaSlicer…" and "Choose my printer".
   - The printer form, with or without a printer chosen: "Import from JusPrin 1…" and "Import from OrcaSlicer…".
   - A link to an app that wasn't found opens the system folder picker, then that app's import screen for the chosen folder.
   - If the chosen folder holds nothing to import, say so in the wording style of board `orca-import-05-no-folder`.
   - The test at `HomeUI/src/App.test.tsx:863-869` checks that no folder link is shown. Kenneth has reversed that decision, so change the test to match.

5. **Add File › Import › Import from JusPrin 1…**, under "Import from OrcaSlicer…" (`MainFrame.cpp:2772`). It opens a dialog like `JusPrin/Home/OrcaImportWindow.*` does for OrcaSlicer.

6. **Look for OrcaSlicer in more places** (`orca_folder()` in `JusPrin/Home/OrcaImporter.cpp:99`, `installed_app_folder` in `AppFolders.cpp`). Add a Linux Flatpak install and a Windows portable install. Look up OrcaSlicer's real Flatpak app id and how its portable build stores data; search for them, don't guess. Keep the `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` override. Don't add a JusPrin 1 folder variable: Kenneth had that removed.

**Rules:**
- Never stage or commit submodule changes.
- Never run bare `git stash`.
- Ask before `git reset`, `git revert` or `git commit --amend`.
- Build with `-j4` at most.
- Put no attribution lines in commit messages.
- If the boards don't settle something the code needs, stop and ask; don't guess.

**Done means:**
- It builds, and the AgentUI tests, HomeUI tests and C++ tests pass.
- You ran the built app through first launch and saved a screenshot of each case. Start it with `HOME` pointed at an empty folder and `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` set as needed. Put a JusPrin 1 copy at `<fake HOME>/Library/Application Support/JusPrin`. See `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md`, "First launch against a staging server". The cases:
  - JusPrin 1 and OrcaSlicer both present;
  - only OrcaSlicer;
  - neither;
  - each Other ways link, including a folder picked by hand;
  - File › Import › Import from JusPrin 1….
- Your final report says, in plain sentences, what changed, what you tested with the results, and what is still open.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_c23b67d2-bb15-4d7d-b393-db6cf7565a2f

# Fork stewardship

**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.

One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**

- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.

Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.

## The ten principles

### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much

**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.

**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.

**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?

**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.

### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge

**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.

**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.

**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?

**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.

### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it

**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.

**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.

**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?

**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.

### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism

**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.

**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.

**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?

**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies our policy.

### 5. One seam beats many touch points

**Rule.** Find the single place every path already passes through, and put the fork's line there.

**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.

**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?

**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.

### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict

**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.

**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.

**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.

**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.

### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly

**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.

**Mechanism.** The real cost of a conflict is not the stop; it is the chance of resolving it wrongly. Appending near an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — keep both — is right. Deleting an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — take mine, the logic moved — silently discards whatever upstream did to that line in the meantime.

**The test.** Six months from now, is the natural resolution of the conflict I am creating the correct one? If not, what does the resolver need to read to get it right, and is that text next to the conflict?

**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.

### 8. Do not diverge where you gain nothing; converge where upstream already went

**Rule.** No gratuitous formatting, reordering, or whitespace differences. Before reverting a cosmetic difference, compare against current upstream — it may have made the same change.

**Mechanism.** Every valueless difference is a conflict site that buys nothing. And if upstream has independently arrived at your version, "fixing" it back creates divergence rather than removing it. Adopting a change upstream has already made converges the two trees early and makes the eventual conflict resolve itself.

**The test.** Does this difference carry meaning? Has upstream already made it?

**Violation.** Consuming a shared blank line in a list of build subdirectories, where upstream also appends entries.

### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it

**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.

**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.

**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?

**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.

### 10. Pull direction dominates every local edit

**Rule.** Replay the fork's own commits onto upstream. Never merge upstream in, and never rebase the whole branch.

**Mechanism.** The fork's own footprint is small; the inherited release-branch history is not. Merging upstream in makes the conflict surface the entire divergence between the release branch and upstream's development line — none of it ours. Rebasing only our commits discards that inherited history by taking upstream's version of every file we never touched.

**The test.** Am I replaying our commits onto upstream, or bringing upstream into ours?

**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main`, which produces a conflict list dominated by vendor profiles, translations, and CI files that JusPrin has never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.

`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.

Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.

`MainFrame`'s Notebook is cheaper to wrap than to dismantle. Dozens of
upstream predicates — menu and shortcut enabling, `can_delete`, slice status
updates, undo/redo gating — key off `m_tabpanel->GetSelection()`, so removing
or reparenting the Prepare/Preview pages breaks them with no conflict and no
error. A shell gets a tabless full-window layout for free instead: hide the
strip via the public `GetBtnsListCtrl()` (wxBookCtrlBase gives a hidden
controller zero size, so pages fill the client area), and the stock slice and
print side buttons disappear with it because `ButtonsListCtrl` reparents them
into the strip at construction. The Phase 1 production shell reached a
19-added-line upstream footprint this way where the POC's reparenting shell
needed edits across eight upstream files.

The same measurement gives the rule for every fork-owned screen that comes
after the shell. OrcaSlicer's surfaces (the stock homepage, Prepare, Preview,
Monitor, the settings tabs) stay inside the Notebook, because their
correctness depends on it. Fork-owned surfaces (the header, the Agent pane,
Home, and whatever follows) live outside it, as siblings of the Notebook in a
fork-owned sizer, shown and hidden by the shell. The shell *reads* the
Notebook's selection to decide what to show and *never edits its page list*:
no `RemovePage`, `InsertPage`, or reparenting of a stock page. Removing or
replacing a page hands the fork the meaning of that index. Upstream keeps
addressing it by number — `tpHome` as a dialog parent, the target of
`EVT_LOAD_URL`, the tab `post_init` returns to — and every one of those lands
on the fork's widget with no conflict and no error. If a fork surface truly
must be a page, append it last, where no upstream code addresses it.

Navigation between screens stays a Notebook selection change even when the
screen being left is fork-owned. Menu and shortcut enabling, undo and redo
availability, and slice-status updates all read `GetSelection()`, so the
selection must remain the one record of which OrcaSlicer surface is active.
Showing Prepare any other way leaves those predicates answering for the wrong
page, silently.

Some stock behavior is already exposed as an event idiom rather than a
function. Upstream itself drives plate slicing from two places with the same
sequence — the slice button and the Cmd+R shortcut both run
`plater->update(true, true)`, post `EVT_GLTOOLBAR_SLICE_PLATE` to the Plater,
and select the Preview tab — so fork code may repeat that short dispatch
without violating the shared-implementation rule; the behavior itself stays
owned by Plater's event handler.

Historical measurements and the incidents behind several of these rules are in the [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) and, for the spike era, in the [POC reference](poc-reference.md).

description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

Links: [{"title":"how to build","url":"https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_build/how_to_build.html"},{"title":"Jack_up da2d2a07b5","url":"https://source.netsyms.com/skylarmt/OrcaSlicer-bambulab-standalone/src/commit/68110eeeccfa77fff3b31cb3e7e4f72ffabd8a26/doc/developer-reference/How-to-build.md"},{"title":"www.git.208concepts.com","url":"https://www.git.208concepts.com/3D-printing/OrcaSlicer/commit/da2d2a07b5ba093e216a92198e2edc41138087db.diff"},{"title":"Aller au contenu principal","url":"https://www.obico.io/fr-FR/blog/orcaslicer-comprehensive-profile-management-guide/"},{"title":"How to build","url":"https://git.208concepts.com/3D-printing/OrcaSlicer/src/tag/v2.3.1/doc/developer-reference/How-to-build.md"},{"title":"Zum Hauptinhalt springen","url":"https://www.obico.io/de-DE/blog/orcaslicer-comprehensive-profile-management-guide/"},{"title":"orcaslicer comprehensive profile management guide","url":"https://www.obico.io/blog/orcaslicer-comprehensive-profile-management-guide/"}]

Yes, OrcaSlicer supports a portable mode on Windows. Create a folder named `data_dir` in the same directory as `OrcaSlicer.exe`, and the app uses it as its configuration directory instead of the default AppData location. The official developer docs describe this, and the setup needs no recompiling. Place a folder named data_dir next to the OrcaSlicer executable and OrcaSlicer uses it as its configuration directory. The main use is running from a USB stick or keeping separate profile sets isolated. Each copy set up this way keeps its own user data.

The docs show the expected layout as `OrcaSlicer.exe` alongside a `data_dir/` folder. A third-party profile guide adds that the default Windows location is under AppData\Roaming\OrcaSlicer, which is what the portable folder overrides. If a data_dir folder exists under the application's path, Orca uses it. The --datadir command line option allows specifying any custom location.

Sources are consistent, and I found no conflicting claims. The search did not cover whether newer releases changed this behavior, so check the current OrcaSlicer wiki if you hit problems.

   - JusPrin 1 and JusPrin 2 share no account. JusPrin 2 can import JusPrin 1's printers, presets and printer connections, very much like the OrcaSlicer import.
   - There are three ways to set up printers: import from JusPrin 1, import from OrcaSlicer, or choose by hand. Each screen links to the other two.
   - When both apps are found, the JusPrin 1 screen opens first.
   - A link to an app that wasn't found opens a folder picker, then that app's import screen.

   - Look for OrcaSlicer in more places.
   Detailed task items:
   1. Stop the start-up copy (`GUI_App.cpp:2464`, `V1Import.cpp`), but keep `v1_folder()`. Keep the scope set by commit a739dc4e7e: printers, presets, printer connections, plus `BambuNetworkEngine.conf`, never app settings. Reuse `OrcaImporter.*`, `OrcaImportLists.tsx`, and the `OrcaImport`/`ImportResult` parts of `Onboarding.tsx`; don't build a second copy. Presets reload after the import.

Remove the "Subscribed to JusPrin v1?" line (`Onboarding.tsx:87-89`). Rework `OnboardingFacts::v1_imported` and `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:430-437`.
   3. Which screen opens: JusPrin 1 found → its screen, even with OrcaSlicer found too. Only OrcaSlicer → the OrcaSlicer screen. Neither → the printer form. A file opened at launch still skips the step. Back returns to the welcome.
   4. Every printer screen gets an "Other ways" line, worded as on the boards. OrcaSlicer screen: "Import from JusPrin 1…" and "Choose my printer", replacing the "Choose my printer instead" button. JusPrin 1 screen: "Import from OrcaSlicer…" and "Choose my printer". Printer form, with or without a printer chosen: "Import from JusPrin 1…" and "Import from OrcaSlicer…". A link to an app not found opens the system folder picker, then that app's screen for the chosen folder. A chosen folder with nothing in it gets a message in the wording style of board orca-import-05. Change the test at `HomeUI/src/App.test.tsx:863-869` ("offers no OrcaSlicer folder…"), since Kenneth reversed that decision.
   5. File › Import › Import from JusPrin 1… (`MainFrame.cpp:2772`) opens a dialog like `OrcaImportWindow`.
   6. `orca_folder()`/`installed_app_folder` also look in a Linux Flatpak install and a Windows portable install. Search for these facts rather than guessing. Keep `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR`. Don't add a JusPrin 1 folder variable.

It has the WelcomeDone line at top, a checklist, "Also brings 3 filaments.", the folder `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin`, "JusPrin starts with X, the printer JusPrin 1 had selected.", an Import button, "Other ways:" with the links "Import from OrcaSlicer…" and "Choose my printer", then Back.

     - The canvas notes `first-run-printer-about` and `orca-import-about` confirm the agreements.

   - Flatpak research:
     - Flathub's current id is `com.orcaslicer.OrcaSlicer`. Upstream commit 73be083ac5 (2026-03-22) renamed it from `io.github.orcaslicer.OrcaSlicer`. The flathub repo was created 2026-03-30.

     - OrcaSlicer uses a `data_dir` folder beside the exe when one exists (GUI_App.cpp init_app_config, ~line 2410).

### First launch against a staging server

First launch looks for OrcaSlicer and JusPrin v1 in their default folders for
the platform (on macOS `~/Library/Application Support/OrcaSlicer` and
`.../JusPrin`), whatever `--datadir` says, and only reads them. Two variables
set up a test run on a throwaway data folder:

- `JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL` names the JusPrin server and wins over
  `jusprin_server.base_url` in the settings file. Use it instead of writing
  the settings file before launch: the v1 import runs only when the data
  folder has no settings file yet.
- `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` names another OrcaSlicer folder; set to `""`, there
  is none. Unset, the real folder is used. On Windows an empty variable cannot
  be set; name a folder that does not exist instead.

v1's folder has no variable. To start as a new person on a Mac that has v1,
point `HOME` at an empty folder: v1's folder is then missing, and
`JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` brings back the real OrcaSlicer folder. The shell and
real-adapter harnesses write their settings file before launch, so the v1
import never runs there, and point `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` at a folder that
does not exist.

```bash
# v1 import and the welcome-back window
D=/tmp/JusPrin2-stg; rm -rf "$D" && JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL=https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io <app>/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir "$D"
# a new person who has OrcaSlicer: the welcome, then the OrcaSlicer import
D=/tmp/JusPrin2-stg; H=/tmp/JusPrin2-stg-home; rm -rf "$D" "$H" && mkdir "$H" && JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR="$HOME/Library/Application Support/OrcaSlicer" HOME="$H" JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL=https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io <app>/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir "$D"
```

### Printer tests without hardware

Bambu paths (printer-menu Idle / Printing / Offline, Select Machine, print job)
are exercised by an in-process fake that substitutes for the Bambu printer
agent while a real Bambu Lab **system** preset stays selected. How to turn it
on, the JSON control file, isolated-instance rules for agents, and acceptance
checks: [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md).

Print-host paths (Moonraker and OctoPrint) run against the real host software
in Docker, with simulated printer boards:
[print hosts README](../../tests/printer_hosts/README.md). Do not add a fake
Bambu network layer (MQTT/FTPS/discovery) without an explicit request.

### Platform matrix

Before release completion, cover:

- Windows with WebView2;
- macOS with WKWebView;
- Linux/X11 and supported Wayland configurations with WebKitGTK;
- supported CPU architectures and a physical GPU where applicable;
- 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling or equivalent platform DPI settings;
- light and dark mode;
- keyboard focus, global shortcuts, clipboard, text selection, and IME composition;
- WebView startup, local resource loading, reload, and recovery;
- streaming scroll anchoring while orbiting and resizing;
- idle and streaming CPU/memory observations.

Classify localized CSS, focus, packaging, or backend problems as platform defects unless evidence shows they require a different architecture.

### Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU

A Windows machine with no graphics driver reports system GL 1.1, so the launcher
(`src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp`) loads `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` instead.
Nothing in CMake or this repository supplies that file or what it depends on, so
provision every freshly configured build tree with
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1`.
Placement is not interchangeable:

| file | goes | because |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opengl32.dll` | `mesa\` subfolder | the launcher loads it by that path; beside the executable it shadows the system GL and the app dies at launch |
| `opengl32.dll` again | beside each `*_harness.exe` | a harness links the app in and has no launcher, so only a copy beside it replaces the system GL 1.1 |
| `libgallium_wgl.dll` | beside the executable | the `opengl32.dll` stub imports it, and Windows resolves imports against the process directory |
| `dxil.dll` | beside the executable | Mesa's `d3d12` driver signs translated shaders with it; Windows Server does not ship it, Windows SDKs carry it under `Redist\D3D\x64` |

Each gap has its own silent signature:

- **No `libgallium_wgl.dll`:** GL falls back to 1.1, the log has `glcontext not ready, postpone init` and no `got opengl version` line, and the canvas stays black for the whole session — the retry after a postponed init exists only on Linux.
- **No `opengl32.dll` beside a harness:** the same GL 1.1 signature, in the harness only. The canvas never builds its volumes, so `Plater::select_object` returns false after `load_files`, and the workspace harness then crashed opening a paint gizmo with nothing selected (`0xC0000005`).
- **No `dxil.dll`:** GL initializes through `d3d12`, then the process exits with `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw, with no log line, no dialog, and no event-log entry. `slow_bootup` only moves this crash from startup to the first canvas paint.

---

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.

---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). ---
name: windows-gui-test-vm-gcp
description: Working recipe for testing the OrcaSlicer/JusPrin GUI headlessly on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP, and the four traps that make it fail silently.
metadata:
  type: project
---

A Windows GUI test VM for this app works in GCP with no GPU. Instance
`jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-central1-a`,
n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB, Cascade Lake), 500 GB pd-balanced,
Windows Server 2022. Harness + full README live outside the repo
at `/Users/kenneth/jusprin-win-vm-harness/`. Verified 2026-09-07 end to end:
launch, screenshot, scripted click, verify the UI advanced.

**Why:** four failure modes here are silent — they look like "the app has no
window" or "the app hung" rather than reporting an error, so they cost hours if
rediscovered from scratch.

**How to apply:**
- OpenGL: the app hard-requires 3.2 and Windows software rendering is 1.1. Drop
  Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` beside the .exe. Then force
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — otherwise Mesa picks
  its d3d12 backend (the GCE virtual display exposes a D3D12 device) and crashes
  on the first frame.
- Never copy the whole Mesa .7z to the VM: Defender deletes it as
  Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere, copy only those, and
  no AV exclusion is needed.
- Session isolation is the big one: display APIs, EnumWindows and
  MainWindowTitle only see the calling session's window station, so over SSH they
  report nothing and it reads as "no window exists". Run anything UI-touching as a
  scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive`.
- Auto-logon must be re-applied on every boot; the GCE image clears the Winlogon
  values after the boot that sets them.
- Resolution needs `gcloud compute instances update --enable-display-device`
  (instance must be stopped) or you get 640x480, smaller than the app's own window.
- WebView2 runtime is absent on a clean Windows Server image; without it the app
  blocks on a modal prompt at startup. Matters especially for JusPrin's
  WebView-based UI. See [[jusprin-rebrand-seams]].

Claude Code and the Claude desktop app are both installed for `guitest`
(2026-09-08). CLI: the native Windows installer `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1`
puts `claude.exe` in `C:\Users\guitest\.local\bin` - no Node needed, the box has
none. Desktop app: install with Anthropic's own Intune script,
`https://downloads.claude.ai/releases/enterprise/intune/Install-Claude.ps1 -Scope User`,
which resolves the official MSIX and verifies its signature and publisher identity.
MSIX deployment works on this Windows Server 2022 image. Launch the packaged app in
session 1 through explorer.exe, so it lands at normal integrity even though the
scheduled task is elevated:
`Invoke-InSession -Exe C:\Windows\explorer.exe -ArgLine "shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude"`.
Electron renders fine on this GPU-less VM with no flags.

RDP: port 3389 is open project-wide via `default-allow-rdp` (to 0.0.0.0/0 - not
narrowed yet), and RDP as `guitest` reconnects to the existing console session
rather than starting a second one. Run `./get-rdp-password.sh` in the harness to
print the current credentials; it resolves the ephemeral IP itself and verifies
the password actually authenticates before handing it to you. Do NOT use
`gcloud compute reset-windows-password` - autologon.ps1 re-syncs the account to
Winlogon\DefaultPassword at the next boot and would undo it.

autologon.ps1 used to mint a NEW random password on every boot, so any reboot
silently invalidated the RDP credentials. Fixed 2026-09-09: it now reuses the
stored DefaultPassword and only generates one when that value is absent (delete
the value and reboot to rotate deliberately). This matters because Windows
Update on this VM is set to install and restart on its own, daily at 3 AM, and
the box has also rebooted unexpectedly several times - Kernel-Power event 41,
cause not established.

Two mechanical traps: nested quoting through `winssh.sh` into `powershell -Command`
mangles almost anything non-trivial - write a .ps1, scp it, run it with `-File`.
And a PATH change made over SSH does not reach session 1's already-running Explorer;
re-set the variable from inside the session and restart Explorer, or a new terminal
there still will not find the command.

Tuned 2026-09-08, both changes measured. Windows Defender had real-time scanning
on with zero exclusions, so it scanned every object file the compiler wrote.
Excluding C:\src, C:\tools, C:\guitest plus the compiler binaries took a
small-file write benchmark from 545 to 983 files/s and reads from 979 to 2257 -
roughly 1.8x and 2.3x, for free. Re-add these if the VM is ever rebuilt.

The boot disk was grown 100 -> 500 GB. On GCE a balanced persistent disk's speed
scales with its provisioned size (140 MB/s + 0.28 per GB), so the old 100 GB disk
was capped at 168 MB/s - it was slow *because* it was small. Aggregate write went
from that 168 ceiling to a measured 262 MB/s. Resize is online: `gcloud compute
disks resize`, then `Resize-Partition` on disk 0 partition 3; C: is the last
partition so nothing blocks the extend, and no reboot is needed.

**Do not benchmark GCE persistent disk with one synchronous writer.** A single
WriteThrough stream is latency-bound and reported only 185 MB/s on the 500 GB
disk, which reads as 'the resize did nothing'. Eight concurrent writers showed the
real 262 MB/s. Use concurrent writers - that is also what a parallel build does.

RDP now prefers the H.264 codec: AVC444ModePreferred=1 (DWORD) under
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services, effective on the
next connection. That does not touch the real interactivity limit, which is the
~57 ms round-trip from California to us-central1; only moving the VM to a west
coast region fixes that.

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on every stop/start.

name: windows-build-on-gcp-vm
description: JusPrin builds and runs on the GCP Windows VM; the five traps that make it fail, and why the CI Windows job failing is a runner-environment problem, not a script bug.
metadata:

---

JusPrin compiles from source on the Windows test VM and the built binary runs
with its Agent UI visible. Verified 2026-09-07 on n2-standard-16: deps 22.7 min,
slicer 23.0 min. Output is `orca-slicer.exe` (261 KB launcher) plus
`OrcaSlicer.dll` (122.7 MB). Full recipe in
`/Users/kenneth/jusprin-win-vm-harness/BUILDING.md`; VM setup in its README.
See [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]].

**Why:** four of the five failures below produce misleading errors far from
their cause, and two were self-inflicted by how the build was driven.

**How to apply:**
- Run long builds as a Windows **scheduled task** (SYSTEM / ServiceAccount), not
  over SSH — OpenSSH kills the process tree on disconnect. Never let two builds
  share a directory: that produced OpenSSL `C1033 cannot open program database`.
- Add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin` to PATH so **awk** is found, or libpng
  cannot generate `pngprefix.h` (`-DPNG_PREFIX=` in deps/PNG/PNG.cmake) and you
  get a confusing `C1083` on a header that was never written.
- Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` for CMake 4.x.
- **Do not use the CI deps artifact** — the shipped bundle predates `deps/Eigen`
  and cannot satisfy Eigen 5.0.1. Build deps from source.
- Never hard-stop the VM mid-build: doing so left 622 installed files full of
  NUL bytes and surfaced as fake syntax errors inside Boost headers.
- Qhull is deliberately excluded on MSVC (deps/CMakeLists.txt), so 24/25 is
  complete on Windows.
- To run headless, use the app's own hook rather than dropping DLLs beside the
  exe: `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` when
  system OpenGL < 2.0. Still force `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe`.

The `Build all` Windows CI job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is a GitHub runner
environment problem, not `build_release_vs.bat` — the same script selects the
same generator on the VM and configures fine against registered Build Tools.

**MSVC rejects `this` in a nested lambda's init-capture.** Found 2026-09-07 at
commit fbe5963b: `CallAfter([self=wxWeakRef<wxWindow>(this),...])` written INSIDE
another lambda compiled on clang but failed on MSVC with 37 errors, because MSVC
bound that `this` to the enclosing closure object, so it tried to build a
`wxWeakRef<wxWindow>` from a lambda pointer
(`Tracked_class_should_inherit_from_wxTrackable`). Name the object first —
`auto* menu = this;` then capture `menu`. Watch for this pattern whenever a
deferred callback is set up from within another lambda; it is invisible on macOS.

**PowerShell splits `-m:6` (2026-10-24).** In a .ps1, `& cmake --build … -- -m:6 -v:m`
reaches MSBuild as `-m:` `6` and fails at once ("For switch syntax, type
MSBuild -help"). Quote them: `'-m:6' '-v:m'`. Also `*>>` writes UTF-16, so
Select-String on that log matches nothing; use `2>&1 | Out-File -Encoding utf8`.
A watcher built from `winssh.sh 'powershell -Command "…\"…\"…"'` silently never
matched for 3 hours — the quoting rule above applies to status checks too.
Killing "my" processes by command-line match also took out a taskhostw.exe;
kill the PIDs your own task started (and their /T trees), not a pattern.

**Shell harness on the VM (2026-11-07, app-menus).** `C:\src\JusPrin\build\tests\shell\Release\shell_integration_harness.exe` has Mesa beside it; run it from a .cmd with `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` through an Interactive scheduled task as guitest; it uses its own temp data dir. Build it with `cmake --build build --config Release --target jusprin_web shell_integration_harness -- '-m:12'` (node is at `C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64`). The VM has no access to unpushed commits: send them with `git bundle create f.bundle <branch> ^<vm-head>`.
- MSVC also rejects a local `constexpr` used inside a lambda that doesn't capture it (C3493; clang accepts). Make it `static constexpr`.
- On jusprin-newui b0a2fe3b08 the default suite already fails 6 checks on Windows: three failed_autosave_* checks (the harness simulates a failed save by removing write permission, and Windows ignores that on folders), earlier_model_version_available, and agent_panel_columns_tile_the_client at 1000 and 1400 DIP. Compare against that list before blaming a change.
- In PowerShell, `[IO.File]` takes relative paths from the process folder, not from Set-Location; use absolute paths. In a .cmd, `echo exit=%ERRORLEVEL%>> f` turns `0>>` into a redirect; put a space before `>>`.

# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

       gcloud compute instances stop   jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend
       gcloud compute instances update jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend --enable-display-device
       gcloud compute instances start  jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend

   Then 1920x1080 is available via set-res.ps1.

## Also required by this app

Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is NOT present on a clean Windows Server image.
Without it the app puts up a modal "WebView2 Runtime" prompt and startup blocks
forever. Installed here as 152.0.4191.66 via the Evergreen bootstrapper:

    Invoke-WebRequest "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703" -OutFile setup.exe
    .\setup.exe /silent /install

This matters more for JusPrin than for stock Orca, since JusPrin's UI is
WebView-based.

## Files

    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../WebShared/*

list(APPEND _jusprin_web_shared_inputs ${_jusprin_web_shared_glob})

# Any further arguments are folders of another page whose source this page
# imports, so a change there rebuilds this bundle too.
function(jusprin_web_bundle name project_dir output)
    file(GLOB_RECURSE _src CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${project_dir}/src/*)
    foreach(_imported ${ARGN})
        file(GLOB_RECURSE _imported_src CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${_imported}/*)
        list(APPEND _src ${_imported_src})
    endforeach()
    set(_stamp ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${name}-node_modules.stamp)
    # npm ci writes node_modules/.package-lock.json. Listing it as OUTPUT
    # means deleting node_modules retriggers the install; the stamp in the
    # build tree is what the bundle command depends on.
    set(_modules ${project_dir}/node_modules/.package-lock.json)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${_stamp} ${_modules}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} ci --no-audit --no-fund
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch ${_stamp}
        DEPENDS ${project_dir}/package.json ${project_dir}/package-lock.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "npm ci (${name})"
        VERBATIM)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${output}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} run build
        DEPENDS ${_stamp} ${_src} ${_jusprin_web_shared_inputs}
                ${project_dir}/index.html ${project_dir}/vite.config.ts ${project_dir}/tsconfig.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "vite build (${name}) -> ${output}"
        VERBATIM)
endfunction()

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

2026-11-02 (connection-skill worktree): adding two new `AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md` files did the same. The jusprin_web target globs that tree, so the build printed "GLOB mismatch!", re-ran CMake and started 945 steps for jusprin_web + agent_bridge_tests + shell_integration_harness.

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake`, and new skill or other globbed files, before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`

name: render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof
description: Have the app draw its own widgets into a PNG for appearance evidence; behavioural assertions miss visual defects entirely, and screen capture is often unavailable.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

For fork-owned wx controls, split painting from the paint event —
`paint(wxPaintEvent&)` builds the DC and delegates to
`draw(wxDC&, wxGraphicsContext&, wxSize)` — then add `snapshot()` that draws into
a `wxMemoryDC` over a `wxBitmap`. The shell harness writes those PNGs each run
(honour an env var like `JUSPRIN_ARTIFACT_DIR`; the harness deletes its temp data
dir at exit, so artifacts written there vanish before you can look).

Note `wxGraphicsContext::Create` has no generic `wxDC` overload — each caller
must build the context for its own concrete DC and pass it in.

**Why:** on the printer/spool chip slice, 267 green harness checks coexisted with
two real rendering defects, both found only by opening the image: a long-name
snapshot byte-identical to the normal one (the capture helper called `refresh()`
first, which re-read the store and undid the test's label — so the width
assertion compared a value to itself), and an inline detail overrunning the
trailing chevron under width pressure (measured width was correct; the overlap
was a painting error). Screen-control access was denied and `screencapture`
could not see the window, so in-app rendering was the only route.

**How to apply:** assert on raw pixel buffers (`wxImage::GetData` + `memcmp`) —
"light differs from dark", "long name differs from normal" — so a silently

Two private artifacts in Kenneth's Claude account mirror the Figma file
([[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]). Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history.

1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9)
   - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`).
   - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel,
     then the coded component. The page lists them as one flat table in bundle
     order with code names; it draws no group headings.
   - `screens/<page>/<screen>.spec.txt` (166) + `screens/index.json`: plain
     files for agents, one resolved line per layer.
2. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
   (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at
   their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark
   mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole.

Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo:
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with
its `README.md` (step-by-step re-sync). `published/` is an exact copy of what is
live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the
scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

What the screenshot comparison caught that file checks could not: dark panels I
had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light
and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear
gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small
frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left.

Other traps: an absolutely positioned layer followed by in-flow siblings paints
over them in HTML (give the later siblings `position:relative`); Figma tints
icons with a mask plus a coloured rectangle; the Artifact tool's bulk read
prints small text files into context, so have a background agent do large
backups; a session scratchpad is wiped on restart — never keep the only copy of
tools there; when two reads of a page exist, keep the later one by timestamp.

Known gaps: photographs and 3D renders are flat placeholders (the 16 worst
scores are all such screens); radial and image fills are placeholders; Figma
stacks 12 dark screens on top of light ones on "Printer & Material Settings"
and the canvas keeps that; ProjectCard and PrinterCard variants are stacked in
Figma and laid out in a row on the canvas; "Add Printer Flow (Obsolete)" is not
read; Notice/Strip drifts a few px vertically.

Figma vs code differences Kenneth has not ruled on (the artifacts hold Figma's):
dark status colours (Figma #4CAF82 / #E07080 / #E8B84A, code #58B894 / #F07A8E /
#E9B960), `radius/full` 10 vs `pill` 9999, Button/Icon 32px vs 26px, Menu/Row
36px full-width hover vs the app's 32px inset rows
([[header-menu-values-kenneth-kept]]). See also [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]]
and [[claude-in-chrome-lives-in-claude-profile]].

Direct editing (2026-10-20): work on a copy of the live files (`figma-mirror/live-<date>` -> `work/`),
publish only the changed files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. The canvas holds its own copy of the
design system in `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens.css/json, components/bundle.*) — change both artifacts
together. `tools/composer/render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome (no type runtime needed);
measure natural board heights in the built-in browser and fix both the board file and canvas.json
(`resize_board.py`). `index.d.ts` must be published with contentType text/plain. The DS card height lives
in the `@dsCard height=` comment. Added then: `surface-raised-hover` (menu-row highlight, dark #3B3047) and
`component-composer-maxLines` (8); the new Composer is drawn by `tools/composer/composer_html.py`.

Publishing (2026-10-20, filament step): a publish is refused as "haven't viewed the latest version" unless this session did a plain `read` of the artifact url (path reads alone do not count). Headless Chrome hangs when another Chrome holds the default profile: pass `--user-data-dir=<tmp>` (render.py now does). MenuRow has `detail`, `detailTone: 'warning'` and `meta` since then.

**Trap found 2026-10-20 (turn line work):** `figma-mirror/tools/bundle.src.js`, `bundle.src.css` and `index.src.d.ts`
were STALE against the live Design System bundle (menu-row detail/meta and the Composer menus had been added
directly in the artifact). Running build_components.py or assembling from those sources regresses the live
bundle. Patch the live files (published/… copies, verified equal to the artifact by sha) and refresh the tools
sources from the patched result; `tools/composer/add_turn_line_boards.py` and the ChatTurnActivity card
were done that way. The DS page generates `tokens.css` itself: never publish it to the DS, only to the
canvas's `project/ds/jusprin/` copy. Adding a coded component = patch bundle.js (function + header list +
__EXPORTS__), bundle.css, index.d.ts (props + window typing), tokens.json, a hand-written
`components/<Name>/preview.html` card with `@dsCard height=` measured by rendering it with React from unpkg,
README.md's component list, and `design-system.json` lastChange in the last call.

**2026-10-26 (setup card rework):** `tools/composer/setup_card_lib.py` draws the two-part card as board markup, spec lines and the coded component from one props dict; `build_setup_card_rework.py` runs the whole rework (cards, screens, calibration, sticky, new, canvas, ds) into `work-setup-card/`. The mirror's `published/canvas` had drifted by three onboarding-v1 boards (fetched back); the live canvas.json, not the mirror's, is the base for an index publish. Version ids before and after each publish are logged in the README ("Versions before the setup-card rework"): the tool cannot list versions, so write them down at publish time. Both artifacts' versions bump when their Artifact type re-releases, so a new version id alone does not mean content changed. `tools/bundle.src.*` and `index.src.d.ts` were refreshed from the published bundle; `heights.json` in the work dir holds every measured board height.

"""Screenshot canvas boards with the canvas's own Design Component runtime, so <dc-import> boards render whole
(render.py draws them blank). Serves <project dir> on a local port with ./support.js = the runtime saved from the
artifact's artifact-type/dc-runtime.js and /_blob/<id> mapped by blobs.json, then runs headless Chrome with its own
--user-data-dir. Usage: render_dc.py <work dir holding project/ and runtime/> <out dir> [--dark] <board.dc.html>..."""
import functools, http.server, json, re, socketserver, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading
from pathlib import Path
args = sys.argv[1:]
dark = '--dark' in args
if dark: args.remove('--dark')
work, out, names = Path(args[0]), Path(args[1]), args[2:]
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
proj, runtime = work / 'project', work / 'runtime'
blobs = json.loads((runtime / 'blobs.json').read_text()) if (runtime / 'blobs.json').exists() else {}
chrome = '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'
class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def translate_path(self, path):
        p = path.split('?')[0]
        if p.endswith('/support.js'): return str(runtime / 'dc-runtime.js')
        if p.startswith('/_blob/'):
            b = blobs.get(p[7:])
            if b: return str(runtime / b)
        return super().translate_path(path)
    def do_GET(self):
        # --dark: the board's theme prop defaults to dark, the way the canvas's Theme switch sets it.
        if dark and self.path.split('?')[0].endswith('.dc.html') and 'board=1' in self.path:
            s = Path(self.translate_path(self.path)).read_text()
            s = s.replace('"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"light"}', '"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"dark"}')
            b = s.encode(); self.send_response(200); self.send_header('Content-Type', 'text/html; charset=utf-8'); self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(b))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b); return
        return super().do_GET()
srv = socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), functools.partial(H, directory=str(proj)))
srv.daemon_threads = True
threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
port = srv.server_address[1]
for name in names:
    s = (proj / name).read_text()
    m = re.search(r'"\$preview":\{"width":(\d+),"height":(\d+)\}', s)
    w, h = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    png = out / (name.replace('.dc.html', '') + ('-dark' if dark else '') + '.png')
    subprocess.run([chrome, '--headless=new', '--disable-gpu', '--no-first-run', f'--user-data-dir={tempfile.mkdtemp()}', '--hide-scrollbars', f'--window-size={w},{h}', '--force-device-scale-factor=2',

`python3 figma-mirror/tools/composer/render_dc.py <work dir> <out dir> [--dark] <board.dc.html>...` serves `<work>/project`, maps `support.js` to `<work>/runtime/dc-runtime.js` (the artifact's `artifact-type/dc-runtime.js`) and `/_blob/<id>` through `<work>/runtime/blobs.json`, and shoots headless Chrome at 2x with its own `--user-data-dir`. 21 boards take about 22 s. `--dark` flips the board's theme prop. A working `work-credits/` exists from the 2026-11-01 credits page.

Also learned drawing that page: anything absolutely placed over the Prepare screen needs a z-index above the composer band's, or the band paints over it. `figma-mirror/published/canvas` is stale (old board names), so pull live files with Artifact read `paths` + `out_dir` rather than copying from it. Cause: every publish to a Claude artifact arms a watch with comment auto-replies in the publishing session.
