9:These steps apply to every change to text a person sees, not only to new screens: a new link on an existing board, a reworded line, or a one-sentence fix all get the cold-reader check on the board before building (step 5) and in the running app after (step 8).
10-
11-1. **Start from the person.** Before drawing, write down in two or three sentences who reaches this screen, what they know at that moment, what they came to do, and what they must decide here. Every line on the screen serves one of those.
12-2. **Draw the whole screen, not a component alone.** A board for review is the full screen at the app's size, with the header, panes and neighbouring content the person really sees there, on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Build it from the Design System artifact's coded components and the app's own markup, never by copying an older board. Repeated compositions are imported by name, as [Design handoff requirements](design-system.md#design-handoff-requirements) rule 9 says.
13-3. **Fill it with real strings.** Text that summarises data comes from the rule that will produce it in the app, run on real data. If only a model could write a line, say so on the board.
14-4. **Write every line by the wording rule below.**
15:5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended.
16-6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer.
17-7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code).
18:8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads.

20:## The cold-reader check
21-
22-The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works.
23-
24-- Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything.
25-- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
26-- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
27-- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.
28-
29-What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three names, "Connected" used for an account). It also raised real questions the review had not, such as what happens after the free month. It has not been compared with a real first-time user, so for the screens that matter most, such as first launch, a person remains the final test.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Earlier work (done before this session): printer-setup-ways commit 9879857a15, the Windows VM check, and merge 473589d032 into ui-walkthrough, pushed.
   - **Current task**, from the parent session `local_c23b67d2-bb15-4d7d-b393-db6cf7565a2f`, relaying Kenneth's approved fix.
     - The bug: File › Import › Import from JusPrin 1… says "JusPrin found filaments or settings in JusPrin 1 that it doesn't have yet…". But it lists only the two printers marked "Already in JusPrin", and Import is enabled.
     - Kenneth wants the sentence and the list to agree:
       - If something new can be copied, list it.
       - If nothing can be copied, say so plainly.
       - Show items that can't be imported with their reason, as the first-launch result screen does.
       - Don't offer Import when there's nothing to copy.
       - Confirm the actual cause before changing anything.
       - Check Import from OrcaSlicer… (same window) and fix it there too.
     - Steps:
       1. Reproduce it.
       2. Update the design canvas board for this window first.
       3. Fix it and add or adjust tests.
       4. Run jusprin_tests, the HomeUI vitest suite and the shell harness.
       5. Commit on my branch, merge into ui-walkthrough and push.
       6. Reply with the commit, what changed, what was tested, and a screenshot of the window after the fix.
   - Standing rules, verbatim from earlier briefs:
     - "Never stage or commit submodule changes. Never run bare `git stash`. Ask before `git reset`, `git revert` or `git commit --amend`. Build with `-j4` at most. Put no attribution lines in commit messages. If the boards don't settle something the code needs, stop and ask; don't guess."
     - "Don't commit submodule changes. Don't rewrite history, and ask before reset, revert or amend."
     - The earlier brief said "Do not edit the canvas"; the new task explicitly says to update the canvas board first.
     - Temporary docs stay untracked.
     - Use the gcloud service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
   - Kenneth wants blunt, plain answers.
   - The new rule in design-guidelines (commit ae8b2fa044): every on-screen text change gets a cold-reader check, on the board before building and in the running app after.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Cause (confirmed by reproduction):**
     - The old `OrcaImportWindow::look()` counted every preset file for which `orca_preset_in_jusprin` was false as new.
     - The only such file was process "0.20mm Detail @MK3S 0.6 - Copy", built on "0.20mm Detail @MK3S 0.6", which JusPrin doesn't have, so its plan outcome is MissingBase.
     - Control run: with that file removed from the JusPrin 1 copy, the window correctly said "Every printer … already in JusPrin, so there is nothing to import." and offered only Close.
   - **Fix:**
     - New `orca_import_offer()` runs `plan_orca_import` with an empty staging path, which plans without writing renamed copies.
     - A printer whose base JusPrin ships but hasn't installed counts as new (`OrcaImporter::missing_base`, made public).
     - A filament or process with MissingBase counts as new while any new printer is on offer, because that printer's profiles may bring the base.
   - **Driving the real app:**
     - Test app `scratchpad/app/JusPrinWays.app`, bundle id `io.jusprin.ways-test`, driven with the computer-use `app_*` tools.
     - Clicks inside the window's web page are refused, because the page runs in another process. Close windows with `element_index 0` (the title-bar close button) instead.
     - The Import button itself could not be clicked.
   - **Builds:**
     - Release build in my worktree `build/arm64`, with the ui-walkthrough diff applied as a patch (`scratchpad/merge-vs-ways2.patch`) and reverted afterwards with `git apply -R`.
     - Debug builds abort on the Mac (OrcaSlicer's PartPlate.cpp GL assert).
     - The Agent page bundle is built in byoai-newui with `npm run build` (vite writes to `resources/jusprin/agent`, which is gitignored). Copy it into the test app's `Contents/Resources/jusprin/agent`, then re-run `codesign --force --deep -s -`.
   - **Canvas** "JusPrin v2" at https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ (Design type):
     - Publish with `root` set to the work folder and only the changed files. Do a plain read of the artifact URL before publishing.
     - Stop the comment watch after publishing (`ArtifactComments` watch on:false; already stopped).
     - Render boards with `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/tools/composer/render_dc.py work png <boards>`.
     - Log each canvas change in `figma-mirror/README.md`.
   - **Cold-reader check:** a fresh general-purpose agent gets only the screenshots, renamed to screen-1/screen-2, plus a user-context sentence.

3. Files and Code Sections (my worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/printer-setup-ways-8564f7`, branch `claude/printer-setup-ways-8564f7`):

   - **`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaImport.hpp`**
     - Doc for `plan_orca_import` now adds: "an empty `staging` only plans, naming each copy in `renamed_to` without writing it."
     - Added, before the `orca_ticked_printers` section:
       ```cpp
       struct OrcaImportOffer {
           std::vector<std::pair<std::string, bool>> printers; int new_printers{0};
           std::vector<std::string> filaments; std::vector<std::string> processes;
           std::vector<OrcaImportItem> skipped;
           bool nothing_new() const { return new_printers == 0 && filaments.empty() && processes.empty(); }
       };
       OrcaImportOffer orca_import_offer(const ImportApp& app, const OrcaPresetFiles& presets, const std::vector<OrcaImportItem>& ticked,
                                         const OrcaImportCatalog& catalog, const std::function<bool(const std::string&)>& installs_base);
       ```

   - **`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaImport.cpp`**
     - In `plan_orca_import`'s rename branch: set `item.renamed_to = renamed;` and then `if (staging.empty()) continue;` before writing the copy.
     - `orca_import_offer`:
       - Printer files (the first `presets.printers.size()` items of the plan): NotImported and not (MissingBase with `installs_base(base)`) goes to `skipped`; anything else goes to `offers(presets.printers[index], outcome == AlreadyThere)`.
       - Then the ticked printers go to `offers(item.name, AlreadyThere?)`.
       - Then filaments and processes: AlreadyThere is skipped; NotImported and not (MissingBase while `new_printers > 0`) goes to `skipped`; everything else goes to `filaments` or `processes` by `item.name`.

   - **`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaImporter.hpp`**
     - Moved `missing_base(const std::string& base)` from private to public, after `profile_catalog()`.

   - **`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaImportWindow.hpp`**
     - `m_printers` and `m_new_*` replaced by `OrcaImportOffer m_offer;`.

     - `look()`:
       ```cpp
       m_source = m_importer.detect(m_app, picked);
       m_offer  = orca_import_offer(m_app, m_source.presets, m_source.ticked, m_importer.catalog(),
                                    [this](const std::string& base) { return m_importer.missing_base(base) != nullptr; });
       ```
     - `state()`: `no_printers` now uses `!m_source.has_printers()`, and the screen comes from `m_offer.nothing_new()`.
     - The payload now has `printers`, `newPrinters`, `filaments`, `processes`, and `skipped`. Each skipped entry is `{kind: orca_import_kind, name, renamedTo:"", imported:false, reason: orca_import_reason(m_app, item)}`.
     - `newFilaments` was removed.

   - **`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts`**
     - `OrcaImportPayload`: replaced `newFilaments?: number` with `filaments?: string[]`, `processes?: string[]` and `skipped?: OrcaImportLine[]`.

     - Added `.orca-import-icon--new { mask-image: url('@resources/jusprin/ui/icons/plus.svg'); color: var(--action-primary); }`.

   - **`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/OrcaImport.tsx`**
     - Header comment lists boards 02 to 07.
     - `Offer` component: shows the printer list if there are printers, then (uncommitted) `<OrcaNewList …/>` if there are filaments or processes (replacing the earlier "New filaments: …" and "New settings: …" text lines), then `<OrcaOutcomeList label="Can’t import" lines={skipped}/>`.

content.text:
The fix is pushed to ui-walkthrough as merge fb032a2ef7. It's three commits on claude/printer-setup-ways-8564f7: 6aa7677ab5, d81750e0b7 and bf2b7f2dc0. Both import windows now match what they list: the sentence, the list and the buttons agree.

**The cause, confirmed by reproducing it:** the window counted any JusPrin 1 file that JusPrin didn't already have as "new". The only such file was the settings "0.20mm Detail @MK3S 0.6 - Copy", which is built on settings JusPrin doesn't have. Import would skip it, but the window still said there were new filaments or settings and turned Import on. When I removed that file from a copy of the JusPrin 1 folder, the window correctly said there was nothing to import.

**What changed:**
- The window now asks the importer what an import would actually bring.
- If nothing can be imported, it says "JusPrin already has everything it can import from this JusPrin 1 folder, so there is nothing to import." It offers only Close.
- Items that can't be imported get a warning sign with the reason under the name, the same way the first-launch result screen shows them. For example: "These settings are built on 0.20mm Detail @MK3S 0.6, which JusPrin doesn't have."
- New filaments and settings each get a row with a plus sign and "New filament" or "New settings" on the right. Before, they were one plain line, and a cold reader took it for the heading of the warning box below it.
- File › Import › Import from OrcaSlicer… uses the same window, so it has the same fix. In my test folder it lists the one new setting and offers Import.
- The design canvas has two new boards and an updated one for this window (latest version 158).

**What I tested:**
- jusprin_tests: 175 of 175 pass, including new cases for what the window offers and a check that planning an import writes no files.
- The AI panel page tests (705) and the Home page tests (158) pass, and the type check is clean.
- The shell harness passes.
- I opened both windows in the built app and screenshotted them (sent above). The files are `import-window-after-fix-jusprin1.jpg` and `import-window-after-fix-orcaslicer.jpg` in the shared notes folder's `printer-setup-ways-screenshots`.

**Not tested:** pressing Import. The automation can't click buttons inside the window's web page.

**Also in the push:** ui-walkthrough on GitHub now includes Kenneth's docs commit ae8b2fa044 about the cold-reader check. It was sitting unpushed on the local branch.

**Wording I didn't change.** The cold reader also flagged existing text, which is outside this fix:
- The JusPrin 1 folder shows as `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin`, which doesn't say "JusPrin 1".
- The reason for settings built on missing settings doesn't say what the person can do next.
- "JusPrin copies them" reads as if the copying already happened.
- Names ending in "- Copy" look like copies JusPrin made.

1. "Below, each item JusPrin can't import says why." It read this as saying every listed row can't be imported, then had to reread because two rows say "Already in JusPrin". The intent is that only the warning row couldn't be imported. Separate the two kinds of rows in the wording.
2. "These settings are built on 0.20mm Detail ＠MK3S 0.6, which JusPrin doesn't have." Both readers had to puzzle out "built on". The row also doesn't say plainly that it was not imported, or whether the person can do anything about it. Both readers asked.
3. The folder line "~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin" has no label. Both readers suspected it was the new app's own folder, which would explain "nothing to import". Say that it is JusPrin 1's folder.
4. The reader in the running app also flagged the current window: "filaments or settings" is vague, and it asked what Import would copy. Your redraw already handles that.

One thing to ignore: the reader also flagged that your board's printers (MyKlipper, Qidi) don't match the printers on the first-launch JusPrin 1 boards (P1S, MK4, K1C). 7:## How a screen gets designed and checked
9:1. **Start from the person.** Before drawing, write down in two or three sentences who reaches this screen, what they know at that moment, what they came to do, and what they must decide here. Every line on the screen serves one of those.
10:2. **Draw the whole screen, not a component alone.** A board for review is the full screen at the app's size, with the header, panes and neighbouring content the person really sees there, on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Build it from the Design System artifact's coded components and the app's own markup, never by copying an older board. Repeated compositions are imported by name, as [Design handoff requirements](design-system.md#design-handoff-requirements) rule 9 says.
11:3. **Fill it with real strings.** Text that summarises data comes from the rule that will produce it in the app, run on real data. If only a model could write a line, say so on the board.

13:5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended.
14:6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer.
15:7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code).
16:8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads.

## The cold-reader check

The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works.

- Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything.
- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.

What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three names, "Connected" used for an account). It also raised real questions the review had not, such as what happens after the free month. It has not been compared with a real first-time user, so for the screens that matter most, such as first launch, a person remains the final test.

## Wording

Every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has.

The five patterns below are what the review found most. Each pair is the text the app showed and the review's proposed rewrite; the rewrites are proposals, not yet in the app.

1. **Facts joined by a middle dot.** The dot drops how the facts relate, and the reader guesses.
   - Before: "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (reads like a balance the person already had)
   - After: "You got 500 free credits for signing up.", with the email address on a smaller line under it
2. **Metaphors.** The reader has to work out what the image stands for.
   - Before: "New or existing account, same door."
   - After: a "Sign up free" button, with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it
   - Before: "Pick how the agent should think." (the options are ways to pay for or connect the agent)
   - After: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
3. **Describing the mechanism instead of the action.** Say what the person does, not how the screen works inside.
   - Before: "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device."
   - After: "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone."
4. **Internal labels.** A name the team uses, shown nowhere else on the screen, explains nothing.
   - Before: "An Expert message is 5 credits."
   - After: the cost in things the person does, for example "500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent" (check the number against real costs)
5. **Hinting at a consequence instead of stating it.** If a choice changes what the person gets, say what it changes.
   - Before: "Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours."
   - After: "Until you add yours, files are sliced for a 250 mm Klipper printer and may not print on other printers."

Space on a screen is tight, and short text looks finished. That is how these lines get written. Shorten only after the full sentence passes the cold-reader check, and check again after shortening.

6. "- Copy" is part of the name, and the warning text also says "It is a copy of". I had to work out that these are two different meanings of "copy".
7. The warning text says "see what you changed in JusPrin 1", but it doesn't show my changes. I may have uninstalled JusPrin 1, and there's no button to show or save the differences.
8. "Similar settings in JusPrin" doesn't say which ones. I wouldn't know where to start.
9. The reason JusPrin doesn't include the original is not given. I now worry whether my MK3S printer works in the new app at all.
10. The warning sign is small and sits beside the body text, not the title. I had to hunt for "the item with the warning sign". The body text is long and in small type.
11. The folder path ends in "JusPrin", which is also the new app's name. I worried it was reading the new app's own folder rather than the old one.
12. "Choose another folder..." doesn't say when I'd need it.
13. The screen doesn't say whether my JusPrin 1 files are left untouched. Screen 2 says OrcaSlicer keeps its copy, but this screen doesn't say the same.

## Screen 2: "Import from OrcaSlicer"

**Every line and button, and what I think it means**

- Title "Import from OrcaSlicer": this window brings things over from OrcaSlicer.
- "JusPrin found settings in OrcaSlicer that it doesn't have yet. When you import, JusPrin copies them and skips the item with the warning sign. OrcaSlicer keeps its own copy.": pressing Import copies the new items over and leaves OrcaSlicer alone.
- "MyKlipper 0.4 nozzle - Copy" / "Already in JusPrin": this will not be copied again.
- "Qidi X-Plus 4 0.4 nozzle - Copy" / "Already in JusPrin": the same.
- "+ 0.12mm Fine @MyMarlin - Mine" / "New settings": this is the one item that will be added.
- "0.20mm Detail @MK3S 0.6 - Copy": this is the same problem item as on screen 1.
- "JusPrin can't import this. It is a copy of the settings '0.20mm Detail @MK3S 0.6' with your changes, and JusPrin doesn't include '0.20mm Detail @MK3S 0.6'. To keep your changes, see what you changed in OrcaSlicer and make the same changes to similar settings in JusPrin.": this will be skipped, and I'd redo my edits by hand.
- "OrcaSlicer's folder: /private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-printer-setup-ways-8564f7/21209ef0-492d-4641-ab5f-85146ab8b348/scratchpad/fl/orca-fake": this is where it looked for OrcaSlicer's files.
- "Choose another folder...": this lets me point it at a different folder.
- "Cancel": this closes the window without copying anything.
- "Import": this copies the new item.

**Where I hesitated or worried**

1. The folder path is alarming. It's a long temporary path ending in "orca-fake", not where OrcaSlicer normally keeps its files. I'd doubt this is my real OrcaSlicer. The path also wraps over four lines and breaks words at the hyphens.
2. The two "Already in JusPrin" items have the same names as in JusPrin 1. If my OrcaSlicer versions differ, are my OrcaSlicer changes silently dropped? Nothing says which version wins.
3. "0.12mm Fine @MyMarlin - Mine" is for a printer called MyMarlin, which isn't in the list. Will this setting be usable without that printer? Should I import the printer too?
4. I can't choose items. It's all or nothing, and the screen doesn't say so.
5. The screen doesn't say where the new item will show up in JusPrin after import.
6. It doesn't say whether imported items stay linked to OrcaSlicer (later edits syncing) or are a one-time copy.
7. It doesn't say whether I need to close OrcaSlicer first.
8. The same unanswered warning items from screen 1 apply here: changes not shown, no list of "similar settings", no reason the original is missing.
9. The opening sentence is built differently from screen 1's, so it took a second read to see that the two screens use the same kind of list.

## Final answers

- **Screen 1:** Both printer items were already in JusPrin, so nothing was done with them, and the MK3S item was not imported. My only option is to recreate my changes by hand on "similar settings", and the screen shows neither the changes nor which settings are similar.
- **Screen 2:** If I press Import, the two "Already in JusPrin" items are left as they are, "0.12mm Fine @MyMarlin - Mine" is copied into JusPrin, and the MK3S item is skipped, while OrcaSlicer keeps all its own copies.</result>

description: "How to drive the real built JusPrin app for a screenshot-per-step UX walkthrough (2026-10-28): scratch copies, the empty local_machines loop with the fake printer, why background app_* tools fail on Orca dialogs, and where screenshots land."

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.

name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

name: drive-app-with-posted-key-events
description: "Drive the built JusPrin app headlessly (even with the screen locked) by posting CGEvents to its pid with a tiny Swift tool; keys work, mouse clicks do not, and the send dialog is reachable by keyboard."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6b96dccc-1cb4-4f72-9de4-3ecee4b28e74
  modified: 2026-09-08T05:58:16.222Z
---

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). Mouse events posted the same way did nothing, even with the window number set on the event.

Inside `PrintHostSendDialog` (Orca `MsgDialog`), focus starts in the filename field; Tab (48) moves to the "Upload" button, Right (124) to "Upload and Print", Space (49) presses it, because Orca's custom `Button` handles Space/Return and arrow navigation itself. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. Watch the app's own `--datadir` `log/debug_*.log` for effects (use `/usr/bin/grep -a`; the default `grep` is ugrep, which treats `\|` literally and may skip the log as binary). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]].

The approved wording is built and pushed: commit d44d66ea71, merged into ui-walkthrough as a9ec334d60. The push also carried the two earlier local commits, a10ac12145 and 9c45c00319. It covers the OrcaSlicer import, the hand-picked printer path and File › Import. I added no tests or checks for the JusPrin 1 import.

**Tests:** all pass.
- The two web-page test suites: 705 and 158 tests.
- The C++ test suite (jusprin_tests): 175 cases.
- The shell harness: both modes (fresh example, switch to the classic view) exit cleanly.

**Built app:** I took screenshots of the Release build on a fresh data folder with a test OrcaSlicer folder, and sent them to you. They cover:
- the welcome screen and "Just slice for now";
- the OrcaSlicer import screen and its result;
- "Choose my printer", empty, then with a Bambu Lab A1 mini picked while "Loading JusPrin's settings for this printer…" shows;
- File › Import › Import from OrcaSlicer…, before and after importing.

**Boards:** the four File › Import window boards on the design canvas now use the agreed reason and folder wording. That is canvas version 162.

**What the fresh reader understood as intended:** the "Which printer do you have?" intro, the skip line, the loading line, the "OrcaSlicer keeps these in…" line and the "Also imported: …" summary.

**Where the reader went wrong or hesitated:**
- **The warning row reads as a failed printer.** The row says "Not imported, because they're based on 0.20mm Detail @MK3S 0.6…". It sits in the same box as the two printers, and nothing on it says it is a print setting. So the reader took it for a third printer that failed, and "they're" read as if it meant more than one item. The earlier sentence named the kind ("a copy of the settings ‘…’"); the approved sentence dropped it.
- **The count on the first-launch screen promises one item too many.** The screen says "Also brings 2 filaments and 3 print settings", and the result then says "2 of 3". The app counts an item whose base it lacks, because installing a new printer can bring that base and only the import itself can tell. The File › Import window follows the same rule, so I left the count as it is.
- **Smaller points I didn't change:**
  - The File › Import window's lists scroll inside themselves, so a fifth row can sit out of sight.
  - The button says "Import 2 printers" and names only the printers.
  - The folder icon is a folder on first launch and a monitor in the window.
  - The test folder's long path shows in the screenshots; a real OrcaSlicer path is short.

**My own additions:**
- The printer version of the reason ends "When you add a printer, choose a similar one instead." The brief gave no printer version, so this is my extrapolation.
- I left the "No printer yet" card on Home unchanged.

Decision needed: should the warning row show what kind of item it is? Today the reason sentence is the only text, so people read the row as a failed printer. One option is to add "Print settings" or "Filament" on the right of the row, the way the new-item rows already show "New print settings". That costs one small layout change in the shared list, plus updating two boards. The other option is to change Kenneth's approved sentence to "these print settings are based on…", which reopens wording he has signed off. Or leave it as it is. My pick is the label, because it keeps his sentence word for word. Should I add the label?

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.

20:## The cold-reader check
55:Space on a screen is tight, and short text looks finished. That is how these lines get written. Shorten only after the full sentence passes the cold-reader check, and check again after shortening.
These steps apply to every change to text a person sees, not only to new screens: a new link on an existing board, a reworded line, or a one-sentence fix all get the cold-reader check on the board before building (step 5) and in the running app after (step 8).

1. **Start from the person.** Before drawing, write down in two or three sentences who reaches this screen, what they know at that moment, what they came to do, and what they must decide here. Every line on the screen serves one of those.
2. **Draw the whole screen, not a component alone.** A board for review is the full screen at the app's size, with the header, panes and neighbouring content the person really sees there, on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Build it from the Design System artifact's coded components and the app's own markup, never by copying an older board. Repeated compositions are imported by name, as [Design handoff requirements](design-system.md#design-handoff-requirements) rule 9 says.
3. **Fill it with real strings.** Text that summarises data comes from the rule that will produce it in the app, run on real data. If only a model could write a line, say so on the board.
4. **Write every line by the wording rule below.**
5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended.
6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer.
7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code).
8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads.

## The cold-reader check

The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works.

- Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything.
- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.

What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three names, "Connected" used for an account). It also raised real questions the review had not, such as what happens after the free month. It has not been compared with a real first-time user, so for the screens that matter most, such as first launch, a person remains the final test.

## Wording

Every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has.

The five patterns below are what the review found most. Each pair is the text the app showed and the review's proposed rewrite; the rewrites are proposals, not yet in the app.

1. **Facts joined by a middle dot.** The dot drops how the facts relate, and the reader guesses.
   - Before: "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (reads like a balance the person already had)
   - After: "You got 500 free credits for signing up.", with the email address on a smaller line under it
2. **Metaphors.** The reader has to work out what the image stands for.
   - Before: "New or existing account, same door."
   - After: a "Sign up free" button, with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it
   - Before: "Pick how the agent should think." (the options are ways to pay for or connect the agent)
   - After: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
3. **Describing the mechanism instead of the action.** Say what the person does, not how the screen works inside.
   - Before: "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device."
   - After: "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone."

content.text:
The new import result screen is built: commit 4890a913ba, merged into ui-walkthrough as 7cbda4e09e and pushed. It shows on first launch and in File › Import, and JusPrin 1 imports use the same screen. The box now holds only the printers that were imported. Under it is the "Also imported" line, without "N of M". Under that, one warning line counts what wasn't imported, with a "Show details" link that opens each item's name and its reason.

**Tests:** all pass.
- The two web-page test suites: 706 and 158 tests. I rewrote the result tests and added one for how the warning line counts items.
- The C++ test suite (jusprin_tests): 175 cases. It doesn't include the import code I changed, so it didn't need rebuilding.
- The shell harness: both modes (fresh example, switch to the classic view) exit cleanly.

**Built app:** I ran the Release build on a fresh data folder. I added a filament whose base JusPrin lacks to the test OrcaSlicer folder, so the run had one skipped filament and one skipped print setting. Screenshots, already sent to you, are in `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-printer-setup-ways-8564f7/21209ef0-492d-4641-ab5f-85146ab8b348/scratchpad/shots/details/`:
- `0-first-launch-before-import.jpg`: first launch, before importing
- `1-first-launch-result-collapsed.jpg` and `2-first-launch-result-details-open.jpg`: first launch, the result with details closed and open
- `3-file-import-found.jpg`: File › Import, before importing
- `4-file-import-result-collapsed.jpg` and `5-file-import-result-details-open.jpg`: File › Import, the result with details closed and open

**What the readers said about each line:** I ran two fresh readers, one on the first-launch screens and one on the File › Import window. Both read every new line as intended:
- **The printer box:** both saw only printers, each marked "Imported". Neither took the skipped print setting for a printer.
- **"Also imported: 2 filaments (…) and 2 print settings (…)":** both read it as the extra items that came across. One found the long run of names in brackets hard to scan.
- **"1 filament and 1 print setting weren't imported. They stay in OrcaSlicer.":** both read it as two items left behind in OrcaSlicer. One couldn't tell whether "stay in OrcaSlicer" is fine or something to fix.
- **"Show details" / "Hide details":** both expected it to show which items and why.
- **Each item's reason:** both read the "It's based on …" sentences as "skipped because its base is missing; pick something similar when you print". Both called "based on" jargon, and both wanted a way to fix or retry.

**Not changed:**
- **Kingroon contradiction:** both readers saw "Kingroon PLA Silk @Qidi…" imported, then read "based on Kingroon PLA Silk, which JusPrin doesn't have". I caused this by naming my test filament's base after one already in the test folder. A real folder rarely holds both names, so I left the wording alone.
- **"New filament" before importing:** in File › Import, the screen before importing lists the two skipped items as "New filament" and "New print settings", and they then fail. That is the existing rule that counts an item as new while a new printer is on offer. I didn't change that screen, and it keeps the long "Not imported, because…" sentence.
- **My own additions:** a skipped printer counts as "1 printer" in the warning line; the brief gave only filament and print-setting wording. Reasons other than a missing base, such as "JusPrin couldn't read this file…", show unchanged under the item's name.
- **Apostrophes:** the reasons under each name use straight apostrophes, as the C++ file does. The line above them uses curly ones.
